prompt: A photograph that looks like a frame from a 1970s British government safety film shot on soft 16mm colour, with visible grain, slightly faded dull greens and browns, and a flat, unshowy camera placed at the foot of a bench press to show what is about to go wrong. In a cramped, cheap municipal gym, a freckled, cheerful young man of twenty-two with a pudding-bowl haircut, wearing a faded blue nylon tracksuit top with white piping, lies on his back on a scuffed vinyl bench press, gripping a loaded steel barbell above his chest and looking straight up and backwards with a trusting, open smile. Behind his head, a tired man of about fifty stands at the head of the bench with both hands under the bar, spotting him: a council-worker face with thick sideburns, thinning hair, a short-sleeved pale shirt and a narrow tie, with a grey gym towel slung around his neck, his expression flat and unreadable. Both faces are clearly visible and in focus, with natural pores, razor stubble, uneven skin and ordinary unglamorous bodies. The light is overcast English daylight from a high frosted window on one side mixed with flat green-white fluorescent tubes overhead, giving a dull, even, slightly sickly cast. Around them are chipped cream-painted breeze-block walls, cracked rubber flooring, rusted weight plates stacked on a wooden rack, and a worn blue crash mat, all out of focus and with no readable text, signs or logos. Medium-wide shot, eye level, 35mm lens, shallow grain-softened depth, muted colour, no gloss. Thanks.
